text:
jordan_support: FYI — ACME reported a sharp latency spike and a few 500s this morning; they say traffic is getting routed to eu-west even though their service is pinned to us-west. attaching what they sent.
jordan_support: repro steps they gave:
1) curl -v -H 'X-Client-Region: us-west' "https://api.redwood.example/generate?model=rw-large"
2) observe 200 normally, but on ~1/50 requests it gets 1000ms+ and headers show X-Redwood-Egress-Region: eu-west
jordan_support: they included this header dump from the failing request:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: redwood
X-Request-Id: req-01ABCD
X-Redwood-Egress-Region: eu-west
X-Redwood-Routed-From: prod-hub-3
```
alex_sre: thanks — can you paste the customer's src IP (or a redacted example) and the `X-Forwarded-For` they see? also want to check SNAT translations on our peered hub.
jordan_support: gave us this: `203.0.113.12` (customer NAT) and Fwd header `203.0.113.12, 10.4.2.11` (we see internal hop). they also said the failures correlate with a cross-region change within 300ms of a TTL expiry on the proxy chain.
maya_platform: hunch: TTL/proxy affinity plus asymmetric NAT could push their request to a peered hub that prefers eu routing when the original sticky entry expired. can someone run `conntrack -L` / NAT translation logs for hub-3 around 08:12 UTC?
sam_engineer: grabbing logs. here's a filtered snippet around 08:11:58-08:12:03 from hub-3 NAT table (redacted):
```
SNAT 10.4.2.11:53412 -> 34.120.45.9:53412 by MASQ (time_left=0)
SNAT 10.4.2.11:53415 -> 34.120.45.9:53415 by MASQ (time_left=120)
```
sam_engineer: interesting — one entry had time_left=0, likely expired and we created a new mapping which routed across the peering to eu hub due to default route preference. that's our window for wrong-region selection.
alex_sre: can we confirm route preference rules on hub-3? I want to see BGP/local preference and any region-affinity policies. also add a quick exploit repro: repeatedly curl with short intervals until hit a mapping expiration.
jordan_support: customer ran a loop: `for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -I ... ; sleep 0.2; done` — they hit ~3/200 failures to eu-west. they want a root cause and mitigation ASAP (customer-impacting).
ops-bot: INCIDENT-4567 created: "support: cross-border egress misroute affecting ACME (hub-3)" — paging eng-sre oncall.
alex_sre: mitigation idea: increase SNAT timeout on hubs for VPC-peered traffic, or prefer local-region egress when mapping not present. can we patch a policy with a short-circuit (prefer local egress if `X-Client-Region==us-west`) and roll in staging for 15m canary?
maya_platform: agree. prefer minimal blast radius: staging -> canary on hub-3 only. i'll draft rollback steps.
jordan_support: relayed to customer that we're working the incident and suggested short-term client workaround: add keepalive noise (0.5s pings) to keep mapping warm until we fix infra.
sam_engineer: I'll prepare a change: bump conntrack timeout for hub-peers from 30s -> 120s and add a routing-policy rule to bias by `X-Client-Region` header when present. will follow change checklist and notify oncall.
alex_sre: capture postmortem template and add perf metrics: p50/p95 latency, percent requests that observed `X-Redwood-Egress-Region != X-Client-Region`, and billing tags for cross-region egress.
jordan_support: thanks team. keeping thread open; will update with customer confirmation after fix. :thumbsup:
